CancelParams.description: The params of a `cancel` notification, written as an object with the id of the request to cancel.

request_id.description: The id of the request to cancel.

Cause.description: Why the outcome has its status: an object with exactly one of the keys `expectation`, `artifact`, `reason` and `legacy`.

oneOf.description: The identifier of the expectation whose outcome this one depends on, under the key `expectation`.
The run-relative POSIX path of the artifact the run did not produce, under the key `artifact`.

A reason code string, under the key `reason`; the codes `not_applicable_to_arm`, `instrument_error` and `deadline` have meanings assigned by the Candler core, and an evaluator's own codes do not reuse them.

A reason code string, under the key `legacy`, for a record whose status, weight or cause the other causes cannot state exactly, such as a zero weight `0/0` on a `pass`; the code says which case. Evaluators never emit it. It is the only cause a `pass` or `fail` may carry, and a zero weight `0/0` requires it.

ContextArtifact.description: One artifact of a run: its path relative to the run, where the evaluator reads it and its digest, written as an object with the strings `path`, `abs` and `sha256`.

abs.description: The absolute path of the artifact, valid where the evaluator runs.

path.description: The path of the artifact relative to the run.

sha256.description: The digest of the artifact's bytes.

ContextRaw.description: One raw stream of a run: its name and the path where the evaluator reads it, written as an object with the strings `stream` and `path`.

path.description: The absolute path of the stream, valid where the evaluator runs.

stream.description: The name of the raw stream.

ContextRef.description: A snapshot or an input of a run: its kind, where the evaluator reads it and its digest, written as an object with the strings `kind`, `path` and `digest`.

digest.description: The digest of the file's bytes.

kind.description: The kind of snapshot or input.

path.description: The absolute path of the file, valid where the evaluator runs.

DescribeParams.description: The params of a `describe` request, written as an empty object.

DescribeResult.description: What an evaluator says about itself in answer to `describe`, written as an object: the protocol it speaks, its name and version, the instruments it uses, its environment, whether it is deterministic, the kinds of check it performs and, when it has one, its reuse rule.

environment.description: The environment the evaluator runs in.

instruments.description: The tools that make the evaluator's measurements.

kinds.description: The kinds of check the evaluator performs.

name.description: The evaluator's name; the plug-in manifest carries the same name.

protocol.description: The protocol version the evaluator speaks.

reuse.$comment: Integers lie within ±(2^53 - 1); JSON Schema cannot state this, and the Rust reader refuses a larger one.
reuse.description: The rule that decides when an earlier verdict can be reused; absent when the evaluator has none.

version.description: The evaluator's version, a `SemVer` 2.0 string; the plug-in manifest carries the same version.

Digest.description: A content digest: `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits.

EvaluateParams.description: The params of an `evaluate` request, written as an object: the run's context, the items to grade, the outcomes already recorded for the run and a scratch directory the evaluator may write in.

context.description: What the evaluator may read of the run.

prior.description: The outcome records already made for the run, which dependent items may read.

scratch.description: The absolute path of a directory the evaluator may write in.

EvaluateResult.description: The result of an `evaluate` request, written as an object with the number of outcomes the evaluator reported.

reported.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; a reader that holds numbers as doubles is exact only below 2^53.
reported.description: The number of `outcome` notifications the evaluator sent for the request.

EvaluatorEnvironment.description: What an evaluator reports about the environment it runs in: the digest of its lock file when it has one, and the versions of its packages, written as an object with `lock_digest` omitted when absent and the map `packages` always present.

lock_digest.description: The digest of the lock file the environment was built from; absent when there is none.

packages.description: The version of each installed package, keyed by package name.

EvaluatorKind.description: How an evaluator reaches a verdict: always the same one for the same input, or not.

oneOf.description: The same input always gives the same verdict.
The verdict can differ between runs on the same input, as with a model that grades.

Evidence.description: A pointer to, or a remark about, what an outcome rests on; at least one of `ref` and `note` is present.

note.description: What the evidence says, a non-empty string.

ref.description: An evidence reference string: `event:<session-id>#<seq>`, or `path:<run-relative path>` with an optional line anchor.

EvidenceRef.$comment: In a line range the first line is at most the last line, and the sequence and line numbers fit in 64 bits; the parser enforces both.
EvidenceRef.description: A pointer to the evidence behind an outcome: `event:<session-id>#<seq>`, or `path:<run-relative path>` optionally followed by `#L<n>` or `#L<n>-<m>`. The session id is non-empty and holds neither `#` nor white space, `seq` is a decimal without leading zeros, line numbers count from 1, and a path in a reference holds no `#`.

ExpectationId.description: An expectation identifier: a letter or digit, then letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`.

FieldPath.description: A dotted path to a field: one or more segments joined by `.`, each a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters, digits or `_`.

Finite.description: A finite real number: neither `NaN` nor infinite. Negative zero is finite.

Instrument.$comment: Each of the version's three numbers fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.

allOf.description: A git digest names the commit of a clean tree.

Instrument.description: The exact tool that made a measurement.

digest.description: What identifies the instrument's content: a `sha256:` content digest, or a `git:` commit hash of a clean tree.

dirty.description: Whether the instrument differs from what its digest names, a boolean; always false for a `git:` digest.

name.description: The instrument's name, a non-empty string with neither `@` nor white space.

InstrumentDigest.description: The digest of an instrument: a content digest, or `git:` followed by the 40 or 64 lowercase hex digits of a commit.

Item.description: One expectation to grade: its id, the kind of check, the parameters and the deadline, written as an object.

deadline_ms.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; a reader that holds numbers as doubles is exact only below 2^53.
deadline_ms.description: The time the evaluator may spend on the item, in milliseconds.

kind.description: The kind of check, one of the kinds the evaluator describes.

params.description: The parameters of the check, as the suite entry holds them.

KindSpec.description: One kind of check an evaluator performs, written as an object: the kind, the schema of its parameters, what it needs from a run and the deadline it gets by default.

default_deadline_ms.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; a reader that holds numbers as doubles is exact only below 2^53.
default_deadline_ms.description: The time the evaluator gives an item of this kind, in milliseconds, when the entry sets no deadline.

kind.description: The name of the kind, as an entry's `kind` names it.

needs.description: What the kind needs from a run.

params_schema.$comment: Integers lie within ±(2^53 - 1); JSON Schema cannot state this, and the Rust reader refuses a larger one.
params_schema.description: The JSON Schema the parameters of an entry of this kind satisfy.

LogParams.description: The params of a `log` notification: a free JSON object that carries one log line of the evaluator.

Name.description: A plain name, such as that of a harness, a reader, a plug-in or a treatment: non-empty, with neither `@` nor white space.

NameVersion.$comment: The major, minor and patch numbers each fit in 64 bits; the parser enforces it.
NameVersion.description: An evaluator or instrument reference, `name@version`, split at the last `@`: the name is non-empty and holds neither `@` nor white space, and the version is `SemVer` 2.0.

Needs.description: What one kind of check needs from a run, written as an object whose five lists are all present, empty when the kind needs nothing of that sort.

artifacts.description: Globs, relative to the run, of the artifacts the check reads.

inputs.description: The kinds of input the check reads.

metadata.description: The paths of the metadata fields the check reads.

snapshots.description: The kinds of snapshot the check reads.

trace.description: Whether the check reads the normalised trace.

OutcomeParams.description: The params of an `outcome` notification, written as an object with one outcome record, which carries no legacy cause.

record.$comment: The record's cause is never the legacy cause; the Rust reader refuses it and JSON Schema cannot state it.
record.description: The outcome record the evaluator made.

OutcomeRecord.$comment: A pass has a weight with num equal to den and a fail has num below den; the schema does not compare the two, and the Rust reader enforces both. The schema states the blocked rule, num 0.

allOf.description: A cause is required for blocked, not_measured and not_applicable.
A pass or fail carries no cause other than the legacy cause.
A not_measured or not_applicable carries no weight.
The weight of a blocked has num 0 and den of at least 1.
A weight of 0/0 requires the legacy cause.
A gate or quality record carries no probability.
A gate or quality record lists no dirty instrument.

OutcomeRecord.description: The result of one evaluator for one expectation of one run, written as an object; `status` decides which `cause` and `weight` the object may carry, and `role` decides whether it may carry a `probability` and a dirty instrument.

cause.description: Why the outcome has its status; required for `blocked`, `not_measured` and `not_applicable`, absent for `pass` and `fail` unless it is the legacy cause.

context_digest.description: A `sha256:` digest of the canonical JSON of the artifacts, snapshots, inputs and metadata the evaluator received.

evaluator.description: The evaluator that produced the outcome, as `name@version` with a `SemVer` version.

evidence.description: An array of the pieces of evidence the outcome rests on; empty when there are none.

expectation_id.description: The identifier of the expectation that was evaluated; it names an entry of the suite.

instruments.description: An array of the instruments the evaluator measured with; empty when there are none, and with no dirty instrument when the role is `gate` or `quality`.

probability.description: A calibrated probability that the expectation holds, as an object; deterministic evaluators never set it, and it is absent when the role is `gate` or `quality`.

request_id.description: The identifier of the request that produced the outcome: a `UUIDv7` in lowercase hyphenated form.

role.description: The role of the expectation, copied from its suite entry when it was graded: `gate`, `quality` or `descriptive`.

run.description: The key of the run that was evaluated: an object with its cell digest, replicate and attempt.

suite_entry_digest.description: A `sha256:` digest of the canonical JSON of the suite entry's `kind`, `params`, `role`, `applies_to` and `depends_on`.

value.description: What was measured, as a value object, if the evaluator reports one.

weight.description: The contribution to a rate; absent means the default of the status: `pass` 1/1, `fail` 0/1, `blocked` 0/1. A `pass` has `num` equal to `den`, a `fail` has `num` below `den` and a `blocked` has `num` 0. Absent for `not_measured` and `not_applicable`.

Probability.description: A calibrated probability that the expectation holds, written as an object with the number `p` and the string `calibration_ref`.

calibration_ref.description: A non-empty string that names the calibration backing the probability.

p.description: The probability, a number from 0 to 1.

ProgressParams.description: The params of a `progress` notification: a free JSON object that tells a person how far the evaluator is.

ProtocolVersion.description: The protocol version a plug-in or the core speaks, written as an object with the integers `major` and `minor`.

major.$comment: Fits in 32 bits; the reader enforces it.
major.description: The major version; a different major is incompatible.

minor.$comment: Fits in 32 bits; the reader enforces it.
minor.description: The minor version; a plug-in may offer a minor no newer than the core's.

ReasonCode.description: A reason code: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits or `_`.

RelPath.description: A run-relative POSIX path: non-empty, with no leading `/`, no empty segment, no `.` or `..` segment, no NUL and no `\`.

RequestId.description: A request id: a `UUIDv7` in lowercase hyphenated form.

ResponseResult.description: The result a response carries: what an evaluator answers to `describe` or to `evaluate`.

Role.description: The part an expectation plays in grading, copied from its suite entry when it was graded.

oneOf.description: A requirement the run must meet.
A measure of how well the run did.
A measurement reported without a verdict on the run.

RpcError.description: The error of a failed request, written as an object with an integer `code`, a `message` and, when there is one, `data`; the code `-32800` is a request that was cancelled.

data.$comment: Integers lie within ±(2^53 - 1); JSON Schema cannot state this, and the Rust reader refuses a larger one.
data.description: More about the error; absent when there is nothing more.

message.description: A sentence that says what went wrong.

RpcErrorResponse.description: A failed response, written as an object with `jsonrpc`, the `id` of the request and its `error`.

id.description: The id of the request this answers.

RpcNotification.description: A notification, written as an object with `jsonrpc` and the `method` and `params` of a [`Notification`], and no `id`.

oneOf.description: An evaluator reports one outcome record.
An evaluator reports how far it is.
An evaluator sends a log line.
The core cancels a request.

RpcRequest.description: A request from the core, written as an object with `jsonrpc`, an `id` and the `method` and `params` of a [`Request`].

oneOf.description: The core asks the evaluator to describe itself.
The core asks the evaluator to grade items.

id.description: The id the response to this request carries.

RpcResponse.description: A successful response, written as an object with `jsonrpc`, the `id` of the request and its `result`.

id.description: The id of the request this answers.

RunContext.description: What an evaluator may read of one run, written as an object: the run's key and root directory, the trace when there is one, the raw streams, the artifacts, the snapshots, the inputs and the metadata. Every list and the metadata are present, empty when there is nothing of that sort.

inputs.description: The inputs the run was made from.

metadata.description: The metadata of the run, keyed by the dotted path of the field.

^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(?:[.][a-z][a-z0-9_]*)*(.$comment: Integers lie within ±(2^53 - 1); JSON Schema cannot state this, and the Rust reader refuses a larger one.
^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(?:[.][a-z][a-z0-9_]*)*(.description: Any JSON value except null at the top, with finite numbers.

raw.description: The raw streams of the run.

root.description: The absolute path of the run's directory, valid where the evaluator runs.

snapshots.description: The snapshots the run was made against.

trace.description: The absolute path of the normalised trace; absent when the run has none.

RunKey.description: The identity of one run: the digest of its cell, and its replicate and attempt numbers, both counted from 1.

attempt.$comment: Fits in 32 bits; the reader enforces it.

cell.description: The digest of the cell the run belongs to.

replicate.$comment: Fits in 32 bits; the reader enforces it.

Status.description: The five-state result of an outcome.

oneOf.description: The expectation holds.
The expectation was measured and does not hold.
The expectation could not be measured because something the measurement needs is missing; it counts as a failure and is attributed to its cause.
The evaluator could not measure the expectation; it is excluded from rates and reported with its cause.
The expectation does not apply to the run; it is excluded from rates and reported with its cause.

StreamName.description: The name of an archived stream: `stdout`, `stderr`, or the name of a collected file, matching `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*`.

Value.description: What an evaluator measured: an object whose `kind` is `number`, `count`, `fraction`, `text` or `counts`, with the payload under the key named after the kind, except that `fraction` carries `num` and `den` directly.

oneOf.description: A finite real number, under the key `number`.

number.description: The measured number, a finite JSON number.

oneOf.description: A whole number of things, under the key `count`.

count.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.
count.description: The count, an integer of at least 0.

oneOf.description: A count out of a total, as the keys `num` and `den` beside `kind`.

den.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.
den.description: The count of parts that were looked at; an integer of at least 1.

num.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.
num.description: The count of parts that were found; an integer of at least 0.

oneOf.description: A piece of text, under the key `text`.

text.description: The text, a JSON string that may be empty.

oneOf.description: Counts by name, under the key `counts`.

counts.$comment: Each count fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.
counts.description: An object that maps each name, a string, to its count, an integer of at least 0.

Weight.$comment: The numerator is at most the denominator; the Rust reader enforces it.
Weight.description: The contribution of an outcome to a rate, written as an object with the integers `num` and `den`: `num` out of `den`, with `num` at most `den`.

den.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.
den.description: The denominator, an integer of at least 1, or 0 in the zero weight `0/0`, which is carried only with a legacy cause on a `pass`.

num.$comment: Fits in 64 bits; the Rust reader enforces it.
num.description: The numerator, an integer from 0 up to `den`.

anyOf.description: A notification, which has no id and gets no response.

description: One line of the evaluator protocol, written as an object of one of four shapes: a request, a notification, a response or an error response.
title: Message
